title: Implanting PDX Tissue into SCID Mice
author: Lindsey Abel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qmpdu5n
materials: Monitor mouse 1-2x a week for tumor growth

steps.title: Prepare PDX Media
steps.instruction: Prepare the PDX media mixture in a 15ml tube (recommended use within 2 weeks).

substeps.instruction: Combine 13.5ml DMEM (e.g., Corning™ DMEM with L-Glutamine 4.5g/L Glucose and Sodium Pyruvate, Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #10013CV)
Add 1.5ml FBS
Add 75ul of 10,000 U/mL penicillin/streptomycin
Add 150ul of 250 μg/ml Amphotericin B

steps.title: Harvest Tumor from Donor Mouse
steps.instruction: Euthanize the donor mouse and excise the tumor under sterile conditions.

substeps.instruction: Place the mouse in a CO2 chamber with the tank rate set to 1 liter per minute
Perform a secondary method of euthanasia once breathing stops
Clean the BSC working area and all required materials with 70% ethanol
Use blunt scissors to cut open the midline of the mouse, ensuring the tumor remains untouched
Excise the tumor by using sharp scissors to make light snips around the base, cutting through fascia and blood vessels to collect a clean tumor

steps.title: Clean and Process Harvested Tissue
steps.instruction: Clean the excised tumor and prepare it for dissociation.

substeps.instruction: Place tumors in a cell culture dish with PBS; rinse and clean further in PBS
Measure tumor size using Vernier Calipers
Transfer the tumor into a dish with PDX media
Move the clean tissue into a 1.5ml tube with 200 μl PDX media

steps.title: Prepare Tissue for Implantation
steps.instruction: Dissociate the fresh tissue (passaged within 48 hours of removal from patient; stored at 4°C) into a homogenous mixture.

substeps.instruction: Place tissue in a 60mm cell culture plate with 2-4 ml cold 1X PBS; trim and clean to remove necrosis, fat, and muscle
Determine if enough tissue (approx. 1g total) exists to save for fast/slow freezing before passaging
Transfer tissue for passaging into a 1.2ml Eppendorf tube with 200-400ul of PDX media
Thoroughly dissociate tissue using sharp curved scissors (e.g., Micro Dissecting Scissors 3.5" Curved Sharp/Sharp, Tungsten Carbide, Roboz, RS-5908SC) until no large chunks remain
Adjust total media volume based on initial tissue weight: 200-350 ul for samples < 0.5g, and 300-400 ul for samples > 0.5g

steps.title: Prepare Tissue-Matrigel Mixture
steps.instruction: Combine the dissociated tissue with Matrigel while keeping the solution cold.

substeps.instruction: Thaw Matrigel on ice; do not allow it to reach room temperature
Add Matrigel to the tube in a 1:1 ratio with the volume of media present
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down 10x or until homogenous
Keep the mixture on ice to prevent solidification

steps.title: Inject Tissue into Recipient Mice
steps.instruction: Perform subcutaneous injections on anesthetized SCID mice.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize mice using isofluorane and prepare the work area
Draw the tissue-matrigel/media mixture into a 1ml syringe equipped with an 18g needle
Place the anesthetized mouse dorsal side up with the nose in a nose cone
Inject subcutaneously in 1-4 sites (100-200ul per site)
Immediately pinch the skin at each injection site for 10 seconds to prevent leakage from the 18g needle puncture

steps.title: Post-Injection Care and Tagging
steps.instruction: Tag the mice and allow them to recover.

substeps.instruction: Apply an ear tag (using ear tag applicator or ear punch) while the mouse is still under anesthesia
Mark the cage with relevant information
Return the mouse to the cage for recovery (should be awake within 2 minutes) before returning the cage to the colony room

steps.title: Monitor and Euthanize
steps.instruction: Monitor tumor growth and euthanize the mouse when the tumor size reaches 600mm^3 or another human endpoint is reached.
